thread:
sre-bot: P1 Incident created — gpu-pool eu-west reported full capacity and sustained queue growth (>12k). Autoscaler attempted but scale-up failed with repeated provider rejections. Pager sent to #incidents and oncall.
ana: I’m oncall for SRE, taking lead. Can eng-runtime confirm if this is autoscaler health or provider quota? @mohit @taylor please ack.
mohit: acked, looking now. grabbing top-level metrics: queue length, pending pods, provider errors. grafana: https://graf.redwood/g/eu-west/gpu-pool
mohit: autoscaler logs show repeated errors: `scaleup rejected: provider_quota_exceeded` and `instance_create_rate_limited`. Also a few `scaleup_attempts_exhausted` from our controller.
taylor: confirmed. autoscaler hit soft limit on parallel instance creations (cloud provider). We also saw higher-than-normal instance boot failures 504 from cloud API. probable combination of quota + rate limits.
ana: Customer impact? @kelsey can you pull top affected customers and error classes?
kelsey: quick summary — 3 tenants see >80% 429s and queued latency >30s: AcmeAnalytics, Flowly, Docsly. Support tickets from Acme and Flowly opened at 09:03. Sending short list in DMs, cc: on enterprise support.
ben: immediate mitigation options: 1) reroute non-critical traffic to backup pool in eu-central (lower perf but available), 2) fall back to smaller quantized model for best-effort traffic, 3) temporarily throttle / reduce concurrency for free-tier requests.
ana: let's do #1 + #2 in parallel. @raz can you flip routing for non-enterprise lanes? @mohit can you start model fallback toggle?
raz: taking routing. running: `redwood route update --from eu-west --to eu-central --selector 'tier!=enterprise' --weights 0.8` — applying now.
raz: route applied. telemetry shows ~65% of non-enterprise requests now going to eu-central.
mohit: enabling model fallback for non-slo classes: `feature-flag model_fallback_eu_west=true` and updating runtime policy to prefer `redwood-v2-small-q4` for fallback traffic.
mohit: fallback live. CPU/GPU token rates dropped by ~30% immediately.
ana: any spikes in error after reroute? graphs?
taylor: queue reduced from 12k -> 4.5k over 6 minutes. Provider errors persist for scaleups but traffic relief looks steady.
kelsey: customer update drafted: "We're mitigating by routing non-critical requests and enabling a lower-latency fallback. Enterprise customers remain on primary pool. We're investigating root cause and will follow up." Want review before sending.
ana: send it, note ETA for next update 15m. flag to CS to manually notify Acme and Flowly.
raz: while rerouting I attempted to request emergency quota bump via cloud console, got automated response about processing delay.
ben: can we spin up spare ephemeral nodes in a different account/az? That takes ops permission but could help.
ana: not safe to change accounts mid-incident. Hold.
raz: got one successful node creation after retry; autoscaler still getting some rejects but node count in pool is inching up. `kubectl get nodes | grep eu-west-gpu` shows +2 nodes in the last 8 min.
mohit: confirming running jobs migrating; KV cache warms slowly. expect tail latency for streamed responses to normalize in 10-20m.
oncall-ml: note — fallback to quantized model will slightly alter outputs. Flag QA/compat for short-term regressions.
kelsey: customers notified. Acme calls our status line, asking SLA impact. I recorded their request IDs and samples.
ana: good. action items for live: 1) maintain fallback + routing until provider stabilizes, 2) throttle free-tier if queue rises >6k, 3) continue pushing quota and follow up with provider. Owners: mohIT (fallback), raz (routing/quota requests), taylor (autoscaler logs & post-incident analysis), kelsey (customer comms).
taylor: capturing logs: `tail -n 200 /var/log/autoscaler/eu-west.log` shows correlated `429` and `503` from provider API at 09:01–09:12. saving to /tmp/incident-1769998888-autoscaler.log
mohit: collecting core dumps and controller state. making snapshot: `redwood diag snapshot --pool eu-west --out s3://redwood-incidents/1769998888/diag.tgz`
raz: provider console now shows 3 pending instance creations, 2 active, rate limit counters resetting. provider support ticket 123456 opened at 09:10.
ana: current status: mitigations applied, queue trending down (4.5k -> 1.2k), most enterprise traffic preserved. keep monitoring. next update in 10m.
ana: handing off to taylor for postmortem and follow-through. Oncall remains reachable. thanks everyone.
taylor: will drive postmortem. preliminary notes: immediate root cause = provider-side rate limits combined with autoscaler not having a cross-region fallback during scale failures. Long-term proposals: add multi-pool emergency spillover policy, improve autoscaler retry/backoff heuristics, add synthetic test to detect provider API limits before customer impact, and document escalation path for emergency quota increases.
raz: adding runbook change: if provider rejects > X scaleups in 5m, auto-trigger reroute to secondary pool and throttle optional tiers.
kelsey: I’ll collate customer timelines and tickets for PMs and legal.
oncall-ml: add signal in monitoring that flags model fallback usage in quality dashboards.
ana: marking incident as mitigated at 1769999208. keep thread open for postmortem comments. :white_check_mark:
